- When sentiment is low (≤0.3), model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a price spike (≥70), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak.
- If recent 3–5 day mean is below 65, model frequently underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% bias upward.
- Sentiment >0.7 correlates with upward bias; adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% if sentiment >0.8.
- Model consistently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) prices; add 0.5–1.0% to final 3–5 days of forecast.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a spike, model fails to correct; apply “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% per 1% sentiment drop.
